entries.original_title: Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain
entries.original_authors: Martucci, K; Borg, N; Macniven, K; Knutson, B; Mackey, S
entries.description: Reduced medial prefrontal cortex (MPFC) response during gain anticipation in fibromyalgia patients compared to healthy controls
entries.citation_sentence: Compared to healthy controls, patients demonstrated reduced MPFC responses during the anticipation of reward gains, but enhanced MPFC responses in response to non-punishment outcomes. NAcc responses during the anticipation of reward gains, however, did not significantly differ between patients vs. controls (Martucci et al., 2018).
entries.notes: The replication found a trend in the same direction but did not reach the corrected significance threshold (p < 0.0125); authors describe results as 'similar trends' and 'consistent with prior results' without claiming clear replication success.

entries.original_title: Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain
entries.original_authors: Martucci, K; Borg, N; Macniven, K; Knutson, B; Mackey, S
entries.description: No difference in nucleus accumbens (NAcc) response during gain anticipation between fibromyalgia patients and healthy controls
entries.citation_sentence: Compared to healthy controls, patients demonstrated reduced MPFC responses during the anticipation of reward gains, but enhanced MPFC responses in response to non-punishment outcomes. NAcc responses during the anticipation of reward gains, however, did not significantly differ between patients vs. controls (Martucci et al., 2018).
entries.notes: The original reported a null NAcc finding; the replication also found no group difference, and the authors explicitly state the result is 'consistent with previous findings.' Per the null-claim rule, agreement with the original null claim is classified as success.
